scenario.bot: 2 teams × 6 seeded bot grubs; 3,000-tick determinism run
scenario.heavy: 6 teams × 6 grubs, scripted napalm/cluster/airstrike/mine_strike/earthquake with seeded graves and props

experiments.hypothesis: Integer terrain-cell indexing and allocation-free collision/proximity scans reduce host tick CPU without changing state.
experiments.change: Use integer cell indexing in Terrain#solid?, fixed-order boolean body collision samples, and short-circuit find in hazard motion.
experiments.metric: Five interleaved heavy six-team A/B runs; tick/step wall distributions, persist guard, CPU/s, and per-tick checkpoint SHA-256.
experiments.reason: Tick p50 is 10.97% lower in the five-run median and wins 5/5 pairs; tick p95 is 7.92% lower and wins 4/5. Step p50 is 12.94% lower, CPU/s is 5.51% lower, all runs retain 16 late ticks, persist size is unchanged, and all 900/900 checkpoint hashes match in every pair.

experiments.hypothesis: The synchronous two-second full checkpoint could dominate a late tick.
experiments.change: Measurement-only investigation; no persistence code change retained.
experiments.metric: Five heavy captures of persist wall/CPU duration and checkpoint byte size.
experiments.reason: Persist is a 4–8 ms wall pause, below the roughly 60 ms terrain full-snapshot spikes. A bounded asynchronous or incremental writer remains an open proposal because save lifecycle and crash-recovery behavior need design review.
